🚨 Meet Rui Wang and Michael Zhang, two former quant researchers who are using financial markets to train AI agents.

Rui previously worked in quantitative research at G-Research and studied Applied Mathematics at ETH Zürich.

Michael worked on high-frequency options trading at TransMarket Group and later worked on LLM inference systems at Etched. 

Instead of building another trading firm, they decided to use the hardest part of trading constantly changing markets as a training ground for AI.

They founded EdotEnv, a quant research lab building reinforcement-learning environments from real financial market data.

7503781304316952576.author: Olena Kocherhina
7503781304316952576.text:
Web3 capital flows shifted noticeably in August 2026, pulling in over $4.51B.

While overall funding stayed strong across 62 recorded deals, the underlying market dynamics underwent a massive structural pivot:

🤌Corporate dominance: Corporate raises took center stage, accounting for around 82% ($3.7B) of total funding, up from July, while venture deals dropped to just 12.2%.

🤌Mega-deals lead: Top corporate raises (Strategy’s $2B+, ZeroStack’s $1B, and Ripple Prime’s $275M) drove 73% of total recorded capital.

🤌AI momentum: Major rounds in Databricks, River AI, and Etched highlight sustained investor appetite for AI infrastructure and compute.

The race to make AI inference faster, cheaper and more efficient is getting increasingly competitive.

Etched is building chips specifically for transformer inference. Positron AI is taking a memory-first approach. Tensordyne is betting on a different mathematical architecture. Then you have Tenstorrent, SambaNova, Groq and Cerebras approaching AI compute in their own ways, while Lightmatter is tackling the connectivity bottleneck through photonics.

7503931416154357760.author: Michael T.
7503931416154357760.text:
Compute efficiency! Not model intelligence is becoming AI’s next moat.
Ben Carden breakdown shows why: even as foundational labs paused mega-rounds, nearly $10B flowed into compute, custom silicon, and infrastructure companies including Crusoe, SambaNova, and Etched.

That capital is chasing the constraint that now matters most: the cost of serving inference at scale. The next AI winners may not be the teams building the smartest models. They may be the ones that can run capable models most efficiently.

你點出的「恐懼驅動」與「新創生存困境」確實是AI狂潮下的真實縮影。

👑 黃仁勳的「30天倒閉」：是心理恐懼，也是統治工具

黃仁勳的「30天倒閉」確實是一種心理恐懼，但這不只是對內，更是對整個產業的恐懼統治。他坦言不想失敗的動力遠大於想成功的動力，這份恐懼讓他維持每週工作7天的高壓狀態。同時，他不斷對外宣告「沒有算力就沒有收入」，將NVIDIA從晶片商重新定義為「AI工廠」，以此建立無法撼動的產業標準。

⚔️ Jane Street 與 Etched：撼動霸權的豪賭

你提到的「Jane Street 新晶片」挑戰，精準命中了NVIDIA的软肋。由三位哈佛輟學生創立的Etched，專注於AI推理（Inference） 市場，在2026年8月獲得Jane Street領投的7億美元融資，估值飆升至210億美元。Jane Street不僅是投資方，更是首個客戶，已收到並開始部署其機架系統。這是一場針對NVIDIA統治地位的豪賭，若成功將直接威脅其護城河。

🌪️ 中國AI新創的「提心吊膽」：殘酷的淘汰賽

中國AI新創確實正面臨生死存亡的焦慮：

· 極高的淘汰率：自ChatGPT發布至2024年7月，中國已有78,612家新註冊AI企業消失。另有數據顯示，23.7萬家新註冊AI企業中，已有8萬家註銷或停業，淘汰率高達34%。
· 融資環境嚴峻：資金鏈斷裂是常態，例如澜码科技創始人賣房發薪。獲得「連投」的企業僅佔獲投總數的2%。
· 巨頭的擠壓：頭部大模型（如DeepSeek、豆包）佔據絕大部分用戶與資源，中小企業只能夾縫求生。

Some great conversations yesterday at Ideas Fest 2026 with founders, inventors and tech businesses reinforced this for me. The decisions made early on around IP can have a real bearing on what a buyer is willing to pay later.  

Can you demonstrate ownership of the technology? Is valuable know-how being captured, or does it sit in a few people’s heads? What stops a competitor replicating what makes the business successful?  

Addressing these questions early helps build a stronger business today and a clearer investment case when the time comes.
